sections.title: Data organization and transactions
sections.text:
**a database.**

A database is an organized collection of data that can be stored, retrieved, updated and managed. For example, an educational platform may store accounts, courses, questions, responses and scores. A database is more than a spreadsheet: database systems can support concurrent users, access permissions, relationships, transactions and efficient queries.

**Main SQL operations.**

| Operation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| SELECT | Read matching data |
| INSERT | Add rows |
| UPDATE | Modify rows |
| DELETE | Remove rows |
| CREATE TABLE | Define a new table |
| JOIN | Combine related table data |
| WHERE | Filter records |
| ORDER BY | Arrange query results |

**ACID properties.**

| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Atomicity | A transaction is completed as a unit or rolled back |
| Consistency | Defined database constraints are maintained |
| Isolation | Concurrent transactions are controlled according to isolation rules |
| Durability | Committed changes persist according to system guarantees |

Actual database implementations differ in isolation levels, replication and durability configurations.

Relational tables contain rows and columns. Primary keys identify rows; foreign keys maintain referential relationships. A payment can require several related changes that must succeed together, so a transaction groups them. Consistency means maintaining defined constraints; it does not prove that every real-world fact originally entered was true. Isolation levels govern concurrency and may provide different guarantees.

Indexes accelerate suitable searches by maintaining additional structures, at a cost in storage and write maintenance. Replication maintains additional copies for availability or scale but can propagate unwanted deletion or corruption. A backup preserves a recoverable state according to its design; restoration must be feasible and tested. These concepts solve different reliability problems.

The State Bank of Pakistan describes Raast as instant-payment infrastructure using ISO 20022 messaging. It illustrates why secure access, reliable communication and coordinated records matter, without revealing the detailed internal design of the entire system. [State Bank of Pakistan: payment systems](https://www.sbp.org.pk/our-operations/payment-systems).

sections.title: Cloud resources and responsibility
sections.text:
**cloud computing.**

Cloud computing provides network-based access to shared or provisioned computing resources such as servers, storage, databases and applications. Instead of purchasing and managing every physical server directly, an organization may obtain computing capacity through a service provider. Cloud services still run on physical computers inside data centres.

**The cloud is not an invisible place without hardware.**

**Five essential characteristics.**

| Characteristic | Meaning |
|---|---|
| On-demand self-service | Resources can be provisioned when needed |
| Broad network access | Services available through network mechanisms |
| Resource pooling | Infrastructure serves multiple users/organizations |
| Rapid elasticity | Capacity can scale up or down |
| Measured service | Resource consumption is monitored and accounted for |

**IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.**

**Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)**

Provides access to computing infrastructure such as virtual machines, storage and networking. The customer generally manages operating systems and applications running on that infrastructure.

**Platform as a Service (PaaS)**

Provides an application-development and deployment platform. The provider manages more of the underlying infrastructure and runtime environment. The customer focuses more on application code and data.

**Software as a Service (SaaS)**

Provides a complete application for use over a network. Examples include many web-based email or office applications. Users generally do not directly manage the operating system or physical servers.

Public, private and hybrid clouds describe deployment arrangements rather than the same distinction as IaaS, PaaS and SaaS. Virtualization separates logical computing resources from particular physical machines. Containers package applications and dependencies while sharing aspects of the host environment. Managed or serverless services reduce some infrastructure administration but still execute on physical systems.

Responsibility is shared according to the service. Even with highly managed infrastructure, customers remain responsible for matters such as application permissions, data handling and configuration. Elasticity does not mean unlimited resources at no cost, and cloud availability does not remove the need for recovery planning. NIST's definition provides the five characteristics and three service-model distinctions. [NIST SP 800-145](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/145/final).

sections.title: Security objectives and common threats
sections.text:
**cybersecurity.**

Cybersecurity concerns protecting systems, networks, devices and information from unauthorized access, disruption, manipulation and other adverse events. It combines technology, organizational controls and human practices. The central conceptual framework is the **CIA triad**.

**Real-world examples.**

**Confidentiality:** A student's private examination results must not be visible to unauthorized people.

**Integrity:** An attacker must not be able to alter examination marks.

**Availability:** A learning platform should remain usable when legitimate students need it.

Security must protect all three.

**Authentication versus authorization.**

**Authentication:** Establishing who a user or system claims to be.

**Authorization:** Determining what an authenticated user or system is permitted to do.

Example: Logging in verifies identity. Granting access to an administrator-only panel concerns authorization. A valid login does not automatically give permission to access every record.

**Common cyber threats.**

| Threat | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Malware | Software designed to cause unauthorized or harmful behavior |
| Virus | Malicious code that can replicate by infecting suitable host content |
| Worm | Malware capable of self-propagating through systems or networks |
| Trojan | Malicious software disguised as something legitimate |
| Ransomware | May encrypt data, steal it or disrupt systems for extortion |
| Phishing | Deceptive communications seeking credentials, money or access |
| Spyware | Software designed to collect information without proper authorization |
| DDoS | Overwhelms a service with coordinated traffic or resource demand |
| SQL injection | Untrusted input changes the meaning of a database query |
| Credential stuffing | Attempts logins using stolen username/password pairs |

Defence combines least privilege, secure configuration, updates, monitoring and recoverability. Multi-factor authentication uses different factor categories rather than merely two copies of the same password. Authorization must be enforced on protected operations, not just hidden interface buttons. Backups help recovery but do not by themselves prevent theft or unauthorized access.

Encryption in transit protects communication channels; encryption at rest protects stored data under specified threats. Hashing produces a derived value and is not reversible encryption. Password storage uses suitable slow password-hashing methods with unique salts, reducing the usefulness of precomputed attacks and identical-password hash comparisons. Secure implementation still matters.

OAuth-style delegated authorization supplies limited access through scoped credentials without giving every application the user's password. Authentication and authorization remain distinct. TLS certificates can authenticate a domain through a trust framework while leaving the site's content dishonest. HTTP/3 uses QUIC, which runs over UDP and provides its own reliable stream and security mechanisms; UDP's basic properties do not imply every protocol built on it is unreliable. [IETF: HTTP/3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9114.html).

sections.title: Governance and public-service resilience
sections.text:
**Six functions.**

| Function | illustrative values |
|---|---|
| GOVERN | Establish cybersecurity responsibilities, policies and risk strategy |
| IDENTIFY | Understand assets, systems, risks and dependencies |
| PROTECT | Apply safeguards that reduce risk |
| DETECT | Discover and analyze possible incidents |
| RESPOND | Act to contain and manage incidents |
| RECOVER | Restore affected capabilities and improve resilience |

The six functions operate as an integrated framework, not a strictly one-way sequence.

The six functions describe an integrated risk framework rather than a compulsory one-pass sequence. Effective governance identifies who can change systems, who reviews incidents and how services recover. Digital identity, payments and disaster warnings require confidentiality, integrity and availability together. NADRA's identity services illustrate sensitive-data management; they do not imply that every person with a valid login should see every record.

A flood-monitoring platform, for example, needs trustworthy sensor records, timestamps, protected administrator access, resilient hosting and recovery copies. Manipulating a water-level record can harm decisions even if the server remains online. Security therefore protects the reliability of scientific information as well as personal privacy. [NIST: Cybersecurity Framework](https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework).

The official [NIST CSF Function glossary](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/csf_function) identifies the six functions.

questions.prompt: In a relational database, a primary key:

options.A: Uniquely identifies a row within the table
options.B: Must always be a person's name
options.C: Contains every record from another database

questions.explanation: A primary key enforces unique row identification.

questions.prompt: What is the principal purpose of a foreign key?

options.C: Connecting records through a referential relationship

questions.explanation: A foreign key references a key in another or the same table and helps maintain referential integrity.

questions.prompt: Which SQL command is principally used to retrieve rows?
questions.explanation: SELECT retrieves data satisfying the specified query conditions.

questions.prompt: What does atomicity mean in database transactions?

options.D: Transaction operations are treated as a unit for completion or rollback

questions.prompt: Why is replication not a complete replacement for backup?

options.A: Unwanted changes or deletions may also propagate to replicas

questions.explanation: Replication maintains additional copies, which may reproduce accidental deletion or corruption.

questions.prompt: Which service model normally provides the most direct customer control over virtual servers and operating systems?
questions.explanation: IaaS offers infrastructure resources with comparatively greater customer control over the software stack.

questions.prompt: Software as a Service generally refers to:

options.A: Owning a dedicated physical power station
options.B: Using a provider-hosted application over a network

questions.explanation: SaaS supplies usable applications without requiring users to administer the underlying cloud infrastructure.

questions.prompt: Which is one of NIST's five essential characteristics of cloud computing?
questions.explanation: Rapid elasticity allows cloud resources to scale up or down with demand.

questions.prompt: The confidentiality component of the CIA triad requires:
questions.explanation: Confidentiality protects sensitive information from unauthorized access or disclosure.

questions.prompt: Authentication differs from authorization because authentication:

options.A: Determines the user's permitted role only
options.C: Verifies identity, while authorization determines permissions
options.D: Always occurs after deleting an account

questions.explanation: Authentication establishes identity; authorization determines allowed actions.

questions.prompt: Which threat primarily uses deceptive communication to obtain credentials or induce actions?
questions.explanation: Phishing is a social-engineering attack based on deception.

questions.prompt: Which NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 function was added relative to the five-function CSF 1.1 structure?
questions.explanation: CSF 2.0 explicitly includes Govern alongside Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Pakistan's Raast system is supported by the State Bank of Pakistan?

options.A: It is a planetary imaging satellite
options.B: It is solely a mechanical cash machine
options.C: It is an instant digital payment system using standardized financial infrastructure
options.D: It is a computer virus detection utility

questions.explanation: The SBP describes Raast as Pakistan's instant-payment infrastructure, supporting digital fund transfers and ISO 20022 messaging.

questions.prompt: Why can creating many database indexes slow some data modifications?

options.A: Indexes are never stored on disk
options.B: Indexes remove all need for SQL
options.C: Indexes may require additional updates when rows are inserted or changed
options.D: Every index must be rebuilt after each read

questions.explanation: Indexes accelerate suitable lookups but impose storage and maintenance overhead on write operations.

questions.prompt: Two simultaneous transactions read and update the same account balance. Which database concern is most relevant?

options.A: Concurrency isolation and prevention of inconsistent updates

questions.explanation: Appropriate isolation and transaction handling help prevent races and inconsistent outcomes from concurrent updates.

questions.prompt: Which mechanism is commonly used to let an application obtain limited delegated access to another service without receiving the user's password?

options.A: Direct transmission of the password to every third party
options.D: OAuth-style delegated authorization with scoped credentials or tokens

questions.explanation: OAuth defines authorization flows supporting limited delegated access; correct implementation and scopes are important.

questions.prompt: Encrypting stored database files protects a different exposure pathway from encrypting communications during transfer. This is the distinction between:

options.B: Encryption at rest and encryption in transit

questions.explanation: At-rest encryption protects stored data under relevant threat scenarios; in-transit encryption protects communication channels.

questions.prompt: Why are unique salts used with appropriate password-hashing algorithms?

options.A: To make passwords directly readable by administrators
options.B: To replace all encryption and MFA
options.C: To reduce usefulness of precomputed hash tables and identical-hash reuse
options.D: To improve a screen's color resolution

questions.explanation: Salts make otherwise identical passwords produce different derived hashes, frustrating precomputation attacks when combined with secure hashing.

questions.prompt: In a serverless cloud environment, which security responsibility commonly remains with the application owner?

options.A: Protecting application permissions, data and code configuration
options.C: Repairing the provider's physical cooling system
options.D: Replacing every data center's electrical grid

questions.explanation: Managed infrastructure does not remove customer responsibilities for application code, identities, data and configurations.

analytical.prompt: Explain relational database architecture, SQL and the ACID properties. Why are these principles important in digital financial systems?
analytical.answer_html:
Introduction

A database stores and organizes data for reliable access and modification. Relational databases represent data using logically connected tables.

Tables and keys

Each table contains rows and columns. A primary key uniquely identifies a row. A foreign key connects records with related records in another table.

SQL

Structured Query Language supports data retrieval, insertion, updating and other operations. Queries can access related data through suitable joins.

Transactions

Financial systems must ensure coordinated changes to balances and payment records. An incomplete transfer can result in inconsistent accounting data.

ACID properties

Atomicity ensures a transaction is treated as a unit. Consistency supports defined database constraints. Isolation governs interactions among concurrent transactions. Durability preserves committed changes according to the system's guarantees.

Pakistan example

The State Bank of Pakistan's Raast infrastructure illustrates the importance of reliable communication, secure authorization, standardized payment messages and consistent transaction handling.

Conclusion

Database integrity is central to modern digital finance. Rapid transaction processing has little value if records cannot be trusted.

analytical.prompt: Explain cloud computing and compare IaaS, PaaS and SaaS. Assess the opportunities and risks of cloud adoption.
analytical.answer_html:
Introduction

Cloud computing provides on-demand network access to computing resources that can be provisioned and released according to requirements.

Major characteristics

NIST identifies on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity and measured service.

IaaS

Infrastructure as a Service provides computing, networking and storage resources. Customers normally manage more of the software environment.

PaaS

Platform as a Service provides managed environments for developing and deploying applications. The provider manages additional infrastructure and platform functions.

SaaS

Software as a Service provides complete applications through network access. Users interact with the software without managing most underlying infrastructure.

Opportunities

Cloud services can support scalability, distributed access, managed databases, rapid deployment and operational flexibility.

Risks

Risks include misconfiguration, unauthorized access, vendor dependence, outages and uncontrolled resource costs. Cloud adoption also creates data-protection and regulatory considerations.

Conclusion

Cloud computing changes how computing resources are delivered and managed. It does not eliminate hardware, cybersecurity requirements or organizational accountability.

analytical.prompt: Explain the CIA triad and assess cybersecurity threats to Pakistan's digital public services.
analytical.answer_html:
Introduction

Cybersecurity protects information systems from unauthorized access, manipulation, disruption and other harmful events. The CIA triad provides three core security objectives.

Confidentiality

Sensitive information should be accessible only to authorized people and processes. Encryption, access controls and appropriate authentication support confidentiality.

Integrity

Information must be protected against unauthorized or accidental alteration. Database constraints, authenticated operations, logging and cryptographic mechanisms support integrity.

Availability

Legitimate services should remain accessible. Redundancy, backups, monitoring and incident-response capabilities support availability.

Threats

Phishing can steal credentials. Ransomware can disrupt operations and expose information. Software vulnerabilities can enable unauthorized access. DDoS attacks can impair service availability.

Pakistan context

Digital identity systems and banking services contain sensitive information and require reliable infrastructure. Pakistan's National CERT provides threat advisories and defensive guidance.

NIST framework

The six NIST CSF 2.0 functions are Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover.

Conclusion

Digital governance requires integrated cybersecurity, not merely installing antivirus software. Technology, policy, professional training and incident preparedness must operate together.
